entities.summary: Pacificus da Ceredano - born Pacificus Ramati - was an Italian Roman Catholic priest and a professed member from the Order of Friars Minor. He was born in unknown year in unknown location, and died on June 13, 1482. Pope Benedict XIV approved his cultus and beatified him on July 7, 1745. Pacificus da Ceredano played a crucial role in the Catholic Church during the Renaissance, and his writings on spirituality and theology were widely read and respected. He was particularly known for his emphasis on the importance of humility and self-denial. Pacificus da Ceredano's legacy can be seen in the many charitable institutions and schools he helped establish, which continue to serve the community to this day. His beatification by Pope Benedict XIV marked a significant milestone in his canonization process, recognizing his contributions to the Church and his devotion to God. Pacificus da Ceredano's story is a testament to the enduring power of faith and the impact one person can have on the lives of others.
